subject: Region instantaneous after cladogenesis is not logical.

messages.author: 7dd62ff152a0f967
messages.subject: Region instantaneous after cladogenesis is not logical.
parts:
Dear Dr. Matzke, 

Thank you for the add. I have been able the run the script without any issues that I can tell (Except for "In (function (npt = min(n + 2L, 2L * n), rhobeg = NA, rhoend = NA,  :
  unused control arguments ignored"

My concern is with the results and was hoping you can have some insights. In a few segments (e.g., P_cau and P_dau, that are in South America (yellow) have and estimated region of South America prior to cladogenesis and for Central America (teal) right after, but both species range in South (Yellow). The same pattern is apparent in the P_orr,P_gil, P_but, and P_hon clade, as well as the clade above it. DO you have any ideas what may be casuing this?

I have attached an example PDF of the DEC, patterns are similar in DIVA and BAYAREA
Also are attached a copy if my scripts and the related data files. I run R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31) in Rstudio

Thank you very much, 

Sincerely, 

Adeljean

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Region instantaneous after cladogenesis is not logical.
parts:
Hi,

It looks to me like you must have switched your tree file somewhere. The Newick file you sent is not the same as the one that produced the PDF you sent.  If you map probabilities from one Newick file onto a different Newick file, many nodes will be mapped with the values from incorrect nodes.

The PDFs I get, with or without the areas_allowed file, seem to look OK. See attached PDFs and script.

(Although -- be sure to search the Google Group to see if the areas_allowed file is doing what you want; it is only useful in certain limited situations, in others you might want to "manually edit" the states list -- see discussion on the Google Group).

Cheers, 
Nick

parts:
Dear Dr. Matzke, 

Thank you very much for your fast response. Thanks you oyour suggestion I figured out where the problem was. I was trying to ladderize the tree to match my phylogeny orientation. In " plot_BioGeoBEARS_results" I used "tr=(ladderize(tr, FALSE))" which caused the issues. It works fine now that I have gotten rid of it. 

I was able to get the right states using areas_allowed file. Just out of curiosity, I tried to manually edit the states, but I could not get it to work. I am new at coding in general and wanted to figure it out for future cases. 

For my case there should be 16 states if it was unconstrained. I entered the example from the Group after the max_range_size setting and the second segment after the call for max size range



# Set the maximum number of areas any species may occupy; this cannot be larger than the number of areas you set up, but it can be smaller.
max_range_size = 2

TF = rep(TRUE, 16)
TF[1] = FALSE
TF[8] = FALSE
TF[9] = FALSE
TF[10] = FALSE
new_states_list = states_list[TF]


# Input the maximum range size
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$max_range_size = max_range_size
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$states_list = new_states_list





Is this remotely how it's supposed to be done?

Thank You, 

Adeljean.

parts: On Mon, Mar 7, 2016 at 3:49 PM, Adeljean Ho <ho....@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Dr. Matzke,

Thank you very much for your fast response. Thanks you oyour suggestion I figured out where the problem was. I was trying to ladderize the tree to match my phylogeny orientation. In " plot_BioGeoBEARS_results" I used "tr=(ladderize(tr, FALSE))" which caused the issues. It works fine now that I have gotten rid of it. 

I was able to get the right states using areas_allowed file. Just out of curiosity, I tried to manually edit the states, but I could not get it to work. I am new at coding in general and wanted to figure it out for future cases. 

For my case there should be 16 states if it was unconstrained. I entered the example from the Group after the max_range_size setting and the second segment after the call for max size range



# Set the maximum number of areas any species may occupy; this cannot be larger than the number of areas you set up, but it can be smaller.
max_range_size = 2

TF = rep(TRUE, 16)
TF[1] = FALSE
TF[8] = FALSE
TF[9] = FALSE
TF[10] = FALSE
new_states_list = states_list[TF]


# Input the maximum range size
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$max_range_size = max_range_size
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$states_list = new_states_list





Is this remotely how it's supposed to be done?

That's the right idea, but keep in mind that the first state is the null range (living in null areas).  If you mean to exclude the null range from the state space, that's fine, but it should be done by setting BioGeoBEARS_run_object$include_null_range = FALSE, since all sorts of annoyingly special things happen in internally in the code, related to the null range.  

Once you've excluded the null range, you would exclude the other states accordingly (making sure you count the indexes correctly; they will all be shifted one).  See how to get the list of states here:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_probabilities



For discussion of what happens when you exclude the null range, see Massana et al. on bioarxiv, the title is something like Non-null effects of null range.

A little more discussion of modifying the state space manually:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/areas_allowed/biogeobears/8UQB_RI_ohQ/R7qJAdh4CQAJ
===================
You can manually edit the states_list, however, to set up whatever list of allowed states you like. This would be done in the R script and not in a text file. See various discussions on the BioGeoBEARS google group, e.g.
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/areas_allowed$20adjacency/biogeobears/7e7U9NtPTBU/pnNtR9M7migJ
===================



Cheers,
Nick

Thank You, 

Adeljean.
